title: Build tags and constraints by file, operating system and architecture

videos.script: Some code cannot be the same on every system. Linux has a signal that Windows does not, and a program that names it will not compile there. This lesson is about choosing which files go into a build. {{line}} First, the go build line. One comment at the top of a file says when that file is compiled. Linux and the other Unix systems, everything but macOS, anything that is not Unix. Put one space in the wrong place, and it becomes an ordinary comment that changes nothing. {{names}} Then file names. A file whose name ends in underscore darwin is compiled for macOS and nothing else, with no line at all. A name that is almost right is compiled for every system. {{tags}} Next, tags of your own. A debug build that says more than the one you ship, and tests that run only when somebody asks. You will also see what a tag costs. A rename passes every ordinary check, while one file quietly stops compiling. {{every}} Last, checking every platform from one machine. A short script vets each system with each set of tags. It catches a mistake that a plain loop over the systems missed.
